data.cleaned_text: 2025, day 198 Good morning from Australia. In markets, President Trump denied he was poised to fire Fed Chair Powell after he showed a letter to fire him to lawmakes, seeing markets whipsaw. He said: “I don't rule out anything, it's highly unlikely, unless he has to leave for fraud.”; Bill Gross op-eds we are closer to inflation fire than deflation ice; In geopolitics, NATO chief Rutte warned of secondary sanctions on India, China, & Brazil over Russia; as ‘Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urges SCO to work for more ‘equal and orderly’ world’ (SCMP) and hit out at ‘hegemonism’ and ‘protectionism’; Lithuania and the Philippines signed a security pact to counter the 'authoritarian axis' of China & Russia; Israel attacked Syria as its troops and/or Bedouin killed Druze, Israeli Druze declared a strike and crossed the Syrian border to fight, Jerusalem reportedly threatened to topple the Syrian government if it continued then, under U.S. pressure, Israel stopped and Syria flagged it would withdraw; and The EU’s Kallas asked Trump to contribute towards the $10bn of weapons it will supply to Ukraine. Italy won’t pay due to budget constraints. France won’t as it’s developing its own arms industry. Czechia won’t as it’s focusing on other military aid. Spain just won’t (as one of its firms just sold military capital goods to Russia). So, only the Germans, Dutch, British, and Scandies will?; In geoeconomics, ‘Forget TACO. Trump Is Winning His Trade War’ (WSJ) as ‘the market is learning to like Trump tariffs’, says Bloomberg. as 10-20% is something they can live with. The FT notes nobody is pushing back and the U.S. is taking in new revenues. Except that’s not where this ends. Tariffs are to raise cash, reindustrialise the U.S., and force a bifurcation from China; as ‘US set to ban Chinese technology in submarine cables’ (FT) where “New rule aims to end key vulnerability in communications infrastructure after attack on American telecoms.”; Canada will impose another 25% steel tariff on all countries ex the U.S. if they contain any element of Chinese steel; Indonesia’s U.S. deal, as expected, doesn’t allow transshipment from China; while France pushes to use the EU nuclear ACI trade countermeasure, likely leading to more than just a trade spat; as Airbus signed a new cooperation deal to localise more production of A321s in China ahead of a key EU-China leaders’ summit - and hopes for a U.S. trade deal requiring less trade with China; ‘Brussels pushes schools to serve ‘made in Europe’ fruit and vegetables’ (FT) where “Change reflects EU effort to favour domestic industries, from defence to agriculture.” So, economic platecraft; An Aussie op-ed from Peta Credlin argues “For the good of Australia, (PM) Albanese should abandon our biggest trade partner to feed the ego of a country planning to tariff our products” - real or parody?; and The House vote passes to advance the 3 crypto bills: GENIUS Act; Clarity Act; and Anti-CBDC Act; as ‘China looks to Africa as testing ground for global roll-out of yuan’ (SCMP) as “A growing list of African nations have made deals to explore or implement use of the Chinese currency for trade and financial transactions”; In politics, Trump lashed out over the Epstein “hoax” again and called those focused on it his PAST supporters whom he no longer requires - but said AG Bondi could realise anything “credible” and —as stated by John Solomon to Steve Bannon— a special prosecutor could be appointed; The European Commission proposed an EU budget of €1.816trn, up from 1.1% to 1.15% of the bloc’s economy, but ‘the European Parliament is already up in arms’ as Germany reached agreement with the EC on a multi-year plan to ramp up public investment now while committing to tightening spending in later years (Politico); and In the U.K., PM Starmer removed the Labour whip from 4 MPs for breaching discipline and 3 further of their trade envoy roles in an effort to assert his control over the party.
